patterns.title: Star of Bethlehem - Shadow Weave
patterns.description: The complete 80-end and 80-pick shadow-weave version in Figure 1, including the continuation. Light and dark 5/2 cotton alternate in both directions; 16 epi. Complementary incidentals adapt the overshot design to shadow weave.

patterns.title: Star of Bethlehem - Rep Weave
patterns.description: Figure 2 uses the same 80-end threading as the shadow-weave study, resleyed to 32 epi. All numbered treadling brackets are expanded. Thick teal cotton alternates with fine 10/2 natural weft. The ordinary drawdown shows the interlacements; the close warp sett produces the rep effect.

patterns.title: Star of Bethlehem - Complementary Plain Weave
patterns.description: Figure 3 reties the original 80-end color-and-weave threading and changes the treadling to create double-faced cloth. Both the main treadling and its continuation are included. Teal and natural 5/2 cotton alternate in warp and weft.

patterns.title: Star of Bethlehem - Woven on Opposites
patterns.description: Figure 4: two repeats of the 40-end Star of Bethlehem pattern, without the shadow incidentals, are threaded in 8/4 cotton at 8 epi. Contrasting teal and ecru worsted cotton alternate in the weft. Includes the two plain-weave header picks and every numbered treadling repeat. Floating selvedges are not heddled.

patterns.title: Daily Drafts - October 3, 2024
patterns.description: Figure 3 is the full 44-end, 44-pick shadow-weave draft developed from Figure 2. Dark and light yarns alternate, with turning-point incidentals as drawn. This is the complete numerical draft, not the adjacent profile draft.

patterns.title: Daily Drafts - October 18, 2024
patterns.description: Figure 5 is the complete 220-end, 220-pick shadow-weave draft, directly transcribed from the printed diagram. It includes two identical 110-end and 110-pick repeats and all turning-point incidentals omitted from the adjacent profile. The color sequence begins with a light weft pick; the first threading end, read from the right, is dark.

patterns.title: Magic Ruffles Scarf
patterns.description: Figure 2: the 22x, 4x, and 22x threading brackets give 192 heddled ends; the central merino wool basketweave strip shrinks during finishing. The color-transition study follows Figure 3; sections marked 42 inches are represented by one four-pick twill unit. Wet-finishing, rather than the flat drawdown, creates the ruffles.

patterns.title: Garden Path Towels - Towel 1
patterns.description: Towel 1: 366 Natural heddled warp ends. The complete colored border, including its continuation, surrounds a plain-weave body unit. The numbered 2x brackets are expanded. Plain-weave hems and the 18-inch body are woven to measured length. Tabby is explicit, not inserted a second time.

patterns.title: Garden Path Towels - Towel 2
patterns.description: Towel 2: the same Natural monk's-belt warp, with the printed Royal and Sage patterning, the numbered 2-2-3-3-4-4-5-5-4-4-3-3-2-2 pattern-pick sequence, and the border woven in reverse. Heather tabby alternates after every pattern pick. The measured-length center is represented by its design unit.

patterns.title: Garden Path Towels - Towel 3
patterns.description: Towel 3 expands the 6-4-6 pattern-pick border, six plain-weave pairs, and 39 repeats of the 2-7-2 pattern-pick body. Tabby is included explicitly in Heather; the plain-weave stripes use Natural. Hems are woven to 1.5 inches.

patterns.title: Garden Path Towels - Towel 4
patterns.description: Towel 4 uses the printed six-treadle tie-up and no tabby. All 2x and 4x treadling brackets are expanded; the body marked 25.75 inches is represented by its complete two-part unit. The issue deliberately weaves this towel wrong side up; invert the tie-up to view the face on a rising-shed loom.

patterns.title: Garden Path Towels - Towel 5
patterns.description: Towel 5 uses its printed six-treadle honeycomb tie-up without added tabby. The 18x bracket and inner 2x brackets are expanded. Natural ground weft, Sage outlines, and Carolina Blue details form the cells. Wet-finishing creates the texture; the printed tie-up shows the reverse on a rising-shed loom.

patterns.title: Misty Mountains Runner
patterns.description: Figure 1 expands the 4x threading bracket across the main line and the first nine ends of the continuation, then adds the three final ends: 179 heddled ends. All 32 pattern picks are included with alternating Naturel tabby. The yarn is a slowly changing gradient; one teal shade represents the supplementary weft here. Border lengths are woven to measure.

patterns.title: Secret Passage Scarf - Eight Shafts
patterns.description: Figure 2 expands the 35x straight threading and all numbered 2x/5x layer-exchange repeats. Complete tube, layer-exchange, and two-layer units are included; sections labeled 17.5, 31, or 4 inches use one unit rather than an invented pick count. Red marks use the second shuttle for the bottom layer. The 4-inch two-layer section forms a tunnel.

patterns.title: Secret Passage Scarf - Four Shafts, Six Treadles
patterns.description: Figure 3 uses 70 repeats of the four-shaft threading and a skeleton tie-up requiring at most two treadles together. Tube, exchange, and separate-layer sections correspond to the eight-shaft project, but use plain weave. All numbered 2x/5x brackets are expanded; measured-length sections use a design unit. Two shuttles keep the tunnel layers separate.

patterns.title: Secret Passage Scarf - Four Shafts, Eight Treadles
patterns.description: The alternative eight-treadle tie-up in Figure 3 produces the same sheds as the six-treadle skeleton notation, with one treadle per pick. The expanded tube, layer-exchange, and two-layer units are retained for direct comparison. Use a second shuttle in the separate-layer tunnel.

patterns.title: Blueberry Waffle Towels - Plaid
patterns.description: Figure 2, plaid colorway. The 42x point threading is fully expanded to 504 ends. Figure 3 supplies the plaid/striped weft order; the variegated towel uses Blue Jay space-dyed yarn, approximated by one blue shade. Sewing-thread hems and the 32-inch body are woven to measure. Floating selvedges are omitted from the heddled draft.

patterns.title: Blueberry Waffle Towels - Striped
patterns.description: Figure 2, striped colorway. The 42x point threading is fully expanded to 504 ends. Figure 3 supplies the plaid/striped weft order; the variegated towel uses Blue Jay space-dyed yarn, approximated by one blue shade. Sewing-thread hems and the 32-inch body are woven to measure. Floating selvedges are omitted from the heddled draft.

patterns.title: Blueberry Waffle Towels - Variegated
patterns.description: Figure 2, variegated colorway. The 42x point threading is fully expanded to 504 ends. Figure 3 supplies the plaid/striped weft order; the variegated towel uses Blue Jay space-dyed yarn, approximated by one blue shade. Sewing-thread hems and the 32-inch body are woven to measure. Floating selvedges are omitted from the heddled draft.

patterns.title: Making Waves Runner
patterns.description: Figure 2 expands all thirteen 5x two-end threading brackets to 130 ends. The fine-weft pairs in A and B are repeated four times per cell. Alternate cells for the 38-inch body and finish with an A cell plus an outlining fabric strip. The four-inch plain-weave hems are represented by one pair unit. The outline yarn is thick fabric; its free side fringe is not represented in the drawdown.

patterns.title: Dicey Dish Towels - Blue Weft
patterns.kind: Fourteen-shaft point twill with plain-weave selvedges
patterns.description: Figure 4 expands the 15x point-threading bracket plus both plain-weave edges to 408 doubled heddled ends (816 individual warp threads). The 24-pick point treadling repeats 24 times, giving 576 doubled picks. Figure 2/3 weft blending follows the published 72/48/.../48/72 pick counts; mixed-color doubled yarns are represented by averaged colors. Shafts 15 and 16 weave the plain edges.

patterns.title: Dicey Dish Towels - Gray Weft
patterns.kind: Fourteen-shaft point twill with plain-weave selvedges
patterns.description: Figure 4 expands the 15x point-threading bracket plus both plain-weave edges to 408 doubled heddled ends (816 individual warp threads). The 24-pick point treadling repeats 24 times, giving 576 doubled picks. Figure 2/3 weft blending follows the published 72/48/.../48/72 pick counts; mixed-color doubled yarns are represented by averaged colors. Shafts 15 and 16 weave the plain edges.

patterns.title: Birds of a Feather Scarf - Six Shafts
patterns.kind: Twill and plain weave with differential shrinkage
patterns.description: Figure 2: a 264-end warp alternates twill Cloud panels and plain-weave colored bands. The 4x/6x threading and 6x/8x/12x treadling brackets are expanded. Black nonsuperwash wool picks (W) shrink during finishing, ruching the bamboo twill areas; the flat drawdown cannot depict that final texture.

patterns.title: Birds of a Feather Scarf - Four Shafts
patterns.description: Figure 4: the four-shaft twill variation has 265 heddled ends plus two floating selvedges. Figure 3 supplies the 32 Onyx, 45 Persimmon, and 188 Cloud ends. Treadling is the same as the six-shaft version, including the W-marked nonsuperwash wool rows. Wet-finishing creates the ruffles.

_omissions: A Shaggy-Bag Story (pp. 22-24): Ghiordes knots on a plain-weave ground; hand-manipulation-only project.
Dip-Dyed Shetland Fringe (pp. 68-72): hand-worked passementerie and dyeing, without a numeric shaft draft.
Yarn Lab Zephira/Zephyr samples (pp. 73-75): photographs and weave descriptions only; numeric drafts are not printed.
Jump-Start Your Designs with Historic Drafts (p. 63): small reference thumbnails and external Handweaving.net identifiers, rather than project drafts.
The reader-guide draft (p. 80) illustrates how to read repeats; it is not an additional issue project.
